headline: Approved bonds, loans, deeds, and license renewals; postponed Project HOPE funding decision to September 14, 2026.
summary: The council approved several municipal quitclaim deeds, a criminal forfeiture fund acceptance, a lease amendment with Hannaford Bros. Co., and a construction contract with Dagle Electrical Construction Corp. It also passed bond and loan orders for sewer system upgrades, and approved two special amusement license renewals. A resolve to fund Project HOPE was postponed to the September 14, 2026 meeting after a proposed amendment to its funding source was withdrawn.
decisions: Approved execution of a municipal quitclaim deed for FALOON real estate at 16 Chase Road.
Approved execution of a municipal quitclaim deed for WALKER real estate at 164 Thornton Road.
Approved execution of a municipal quitclaim deed for CARSON real estate at 248 Randolph Drive.
Approved execution of a municipal quitclaim deed for WALKER real estate at 849 Stillwater Avenue.
Approved accepting $6,090 in funds from a state criminal forfeiture.
Approved an amended lease agreement between the City of Bangor and Hannaford Bros. Co., LLC for property at 39 Florida Avenue.
Approved a construction contract with Dagle Electrical Construction Corp. for traffic signal improvements at Broadway and Stillwater Avenue.
Passed issuance of $4,455,000 in General Obligation Bonds for KMart Pump Station and sewer infrastructure improvements, 9-0.
Passed a $6,575,000 loan from the Maine Municipal Bond Bank State Revolving Fund for Perry Road Pump Station replacement, 9-0.
Withdrew a motion to amend the title and funding source language of the Project HOPE resolve.
Postponed the Project HOPE funding resolve to the September 14, 2026 council meeting, 9-0.
Approved the Special Amusement License renewal for Timka, Inc., d/b/a Geaghan's Pub, 570 Main Street, 9-0.
Approved the Special Amusement License renewal for Global Spectrum LP d/b/a Cross Insurance Center, 515 Main Street, 9-0.

Who We Can'Contact in LasVegasfor;Guidance
The Courtyard HomelessResourceCenter is operated by the City of LasVegas. We can reach out
to their team for guidance on how they built their model and what lessons they' ve learned.
Contact Information:
Phone: 702- 229- 6117
Email: courtyardHRC@lasvegasnevada. gov
Address: 314 Foremaster Lane, Las Vegas, NV 89101
Website: lasvegasnevada. gov
They also work with the MORE Team ( Multi- Agency Outreach Resource Engagement), which
handles mobile outreach and encampment response:
Phone: 702- 229- 6673
We can ask for`: 
Planning documents and blueprints
Funding sources and partnership strategies
Implementation challenges and solutions
Community feedback and impact data
Advice on adapfing the model to Bangor' s climate and layout
How Other Cifies Have Implemented Similar ldeas
Cities that have adopted Courtyard- style or low- barrier service hubs often follow these steps:
1. Needs Assessment
We conduct local research to identify gaps in daytime shelter, sanitation, outreach, and
safety
Our observation and survey work already provide a strong foundation
2. Stakeholder Engagement
We meet with city officials, shelter directors, public health teams, and police
We include voices of unhoused individuals and service providers
3. Site Selection
We identify a location near existing services ( Coes Pond Park is a strong candidate)
We consider zoning, accessibility, and environmental impact
4. Partnership Building
We collaborate with nonprofits, hospitals, mental health providers, and housing
agencies
We seek support from city council, planning boards, and community leaders
5. Funding Strategy L
We explore city funds, federal grants ( HUD, HHS), and private donations
We look into ARPA funds or Continuum of Care grants
6. Pilot Phase
We begin with basic services: rest area, bathrooms, outreach
We expand to include storage, medical care, pet support, and housing navigation

We draft a student- led proposal outlining the Courtyard model and its benefits
We host a community listening sessionto gather feedback
We create a visual layout of the proposed space at Coes Pond Park
We present findings to the Advisory Committee and City Council
